title: Real English to Speak when you Travel - Advanced Slow English Podcast

sentences.en: Hello and welcome back to my Slow English podcast. I am visiting China right now. And if you didn't know, I have been learning Chinese for about 3 years now. But honestly, nothing prepared me for the Chinese that I would actually need in China. The real life Chinese. The words that help you sound natural, blend in, and even get those little compliments from locals. There's something really special about being in a country. and actually connecting with people in their own language. It feels so good to see someone be genuinely surprised or impressed when you can speak to them, even just a little. And it's such a nice feeling when you can finally understand the little phrases and just the way people here really speak. All those tiny things help you sound more polite, natural, respectful, and confident. My sister Brianna is going to help me walk through each scenario. Now, if you're ever lost and you need to ask for directions, you can say, "Excuse me, I am lost. Do you know where this is?" Whatever you need to find. Excuse me. Do you know where the ATM is? Yes, there's one two blocks down on this road. Great. Thanks a lot. That's a better way of asking for directions. Most native English speakers would ask this way. They wouldn't say, "Where.
